html:
Theravada, "the teaching of the elders", is the oldest surviving school of Buddhism. It is the main religion of Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia, and holds about a third of the world's Buddhists.

It keeps the teaching of the Buddha in the Pali Canon, written in Pali, an old Indian language. Its ideal is the monk who follows the Buddha's path to free himself from rebirth. Monks keep strict rules, beg for their food each morning and depend on lay people, who gain merit by giving. It is more conservative than the Mahayana schools of East Asia and Tibet.

Its story runs through Sri Lanka:

  • In the 200s BCE, by tradition, Mahinda, son of the emperor Ashoka, brought Buddhism to the island; see Sinhala.
  • Around the 1st century BCE monks there wrote down the Pali Canon.
  • From Sri Lanka the tradition spread to mainland Southeast Asia. The Mon of Dvaravati were early followers. King Anawrahta adopted it at Pagan in Burma in the 1000s, and Ramkhamhaeng of Sukhothai backed monks of the Sri Lankan line.

Kings in these lands used it to show their virtue, and reformed its monks when they seemed lax. In Siam, Prince Mongkut founded the stricter Dhammayuttika order in the 1830s.
sum: Theravada, "the teaching of the elders", is the oldest surviving school of Buddhism. It is the main religion of Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia, and holds about a third of the world's Buddhists.
